rationale: C15 plausibly supplied material compensation-setting machinery for the child: both address federal positions outside ordinary Classification Act treatment, assign compensation administration across departments or establishments, and impose a ceiling tied to Classification Act rates. The child adapts that machinery to patient-filled hospital positions and makes the ceiling more directly position-specific. C02 has related compensation administration and exact first-pay-period language, while C24 supplies a close policy predicate concerning hospital positions and limits on administratively set pay, but neither is as close a reusable operative template as C15.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Unless otherwise provided by law, the rates of compensation for such positions shall be determined by the heads of the respective departments and independent establishments
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the payment of salaries and compensation ... shall be made by the several executive departments, independent establishments, and corporations
shared_material.explanation: Both distribute responsibility for administering compensation among the affected federal departments and establishments.

shared_material.child_excerpt: No such rate of compensation shall exceed the rate which would be applicable to the position if it had remained under the provisions of the Classification Act of 1923, as amended.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: no such salary or compensation shall exceed the maximum provided by the Classification Act of 1923, as amended
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive shared ceiling mechanism tying administratively determined compensation to limits under the same named Classification Act.
